availableCommands.name: architecture-diagrams
availableCommands.description: Author, render, and verify kora architecture diagrams. Excalidraw sources under docs/diagrams/ render to committed SVGs via tools/diagrams (make diagrams / make check); sequences are inline Mermaid. Covers the full loop: generate the scene, render, self-verify the PNG at natural size, adversarially review it against the code and the already-approved diagrams, then wire it into the docs. Use when asked to create, update, or review an architecture diagram, a system/context/topology diagram, or a docs/architecture page.

availableCommands.name: customize-opencode
availableCommands.description: Use ONLY when the user is editing or creating opencode's own configuration: opencode.json, opencode.jsonc, files under .opencode/, or files under ~/.config/opencode/. Also use when creating or fixing opencode agents, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers, or permission rules. Do not use for the user's own application code, or for any project that is not configuring opencode itself.

availableCommands.name: new-feature
availableCommands.description: Kick off a new kora feature the disciplined way — a guided, planning-only workflow that produces an approved PRD and an approved, indexed ADR, ready to hand off to implementation. Runs an accessible interview (no jargon), drafts docs/prd/{slug}.md from the template, hard-stops for approval, then drafts docs/adr/{date}-{slug}.md, registers it in the ADR index, and hard-stops again. Creates a feature branch if on main. Use when asked to "start a new feature", "kick off a feature", "begin the feature workflow", "write a PRD", "create an ADR", or to scope/plan a new capability before any code is written. Stops before implementation — it plans, it does not build.

availableCommands.name: ui-component
availableCommands.description: Create new UI components, promote existing ones across tiers, or verify a component is in the right tier. Applies the three-tier placement decision tree (Hades / App-shared / Feature-scoped), implements with correct patterns (forwardRef, cva, cn, data-slot, @tier JSDoc), and produces or updates the co-located Storybook story. Use when asked to "add a component", "create a component", "promote a component", "check the tier", "wire up Storybook", "what tier does this belong to", "should this be promoted", or when reviewing a Tier 2 or Tier 3 component for potential promotion. TRIGGER — invoke this skill before creating, modifying, or reviewing any component file under frontend/src/; do not skip because the task looks like a one-liner.

availableCommands.name: verify-prs
availableCommands.description: Triage, locally verify, and drive open GitHub PRs (especially agent/bot-authored ones) toward merge in the kora repo. Inventory + audit the queue, deploy each branch to the local k3d cluster and exercise REAL behaviour (not just CI), fix lint/tests/review-comments, then merge / close-as-duplicate / send back with documented findings. Use when asked to review, triage, "babysit", or shepherd open PRs, to "get PRs merged", to verify a PR locally, or to process the PR backlog.
